text.p: Parliament resolved a deadlock on Thursday with a compromise over a proposed bill to introduce protective tariffs.

The deadlock, which saw right-wing opposition parliamentarians use delaying tactics late into Wednesday night to hold off debate on the tariffs, ended when government parties and the opposition agreed to postpone the debate until August.
"We reached a compromise which will give a two month stabilisation period," Tunne Kelam, parliamentary deputy speaker, told Reuters.
"We are very happy as we had planned for our working day to last until midnight," he added.
The controversial bill would have seen the introduction of protective tariffs on imported pork as a response to the agricultural lobby.

"The compromise agreement means that the coalition government parties will consider an amendment which will determine if the the government or the parliament has the right to impose protective tariffs," Kelam added.
Opposition parties agreed to debate the issue again at an extraordinary session at the end of August and not to use delaying tactics again during the debate.
Estonia has long prided itself on being a free trade state and the introduction of tariffs to protect a weaken agricultural sector remains a hotly debated topic.
